notation.meaning: Average of $Y$ for a given value of $X$
Overall mean and mean in group $g$
Errors and regressors in the econometrics applications

blocks.md: The law of iterated expectations says that an overall average equals the average of group averages, each weighted by the size of its group. If two-thirds of workers earn 30 dollars an hour on average and one-third earn 60, the overall average is 40. In probability language: first average within each value of one variable, then average those averages, and you recover the plain average.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.md: It sits behind many proofs in econometrics — including why an error unrelated to the regressors on average is also uncorrelated with them — and behind every composition effect in labor data.
The average of the conditional averages is the overall average, weighting each group by its probability.

| Course | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Econometrics | One-line proof that $E[\varepsilon\mid\mathbf{X}] = 0$ implies $\mathrm{Cov}(\mathbf{X},\varepsilon) = 0$ ([Strict Exogeneity](note:strict-exogeneity)) |
| Econometrics | Unbiasedness of OLS: condition on $\mathbf{X}$, then average ([OLS Estimator](note:ols-estimator)) |
| Inequality | An overall average wage is a weighted average of group averages — the root of composition effects ([Composition Adjustment](note:composition-adjustment)) |
| Probability | Building block of the [Law of Total Variance](note:law-of-total-variance) |
